mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through lower cost of capital for corporate earnings. This relationship holds consistently without regime-specific conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation, triggering Federal Reserve monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL YoY change is negative.

mechanism_narrative: The joint growth of labor market strength (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) above 12-month moving averages signals sustained economic expansion, creating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through earnings momentum. The interaction effect is non-linear and requires both series to exceed thresholds.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * RSAFS) fails to produce a statistically significant positive correlation with 20-day S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05) in any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and HOUST > 1200 thousand units), overheating signals trigger monetary tightening, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to profit margin compression and valuation resets.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% and HOUST exceeds 1200, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through short-term momentum effects.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 5-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals labor market tightness, increasing wage pressures and inflation expectations, which leads to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to extended monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: The 60-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of high FEDFUNDS (> 4.0%) and high CPIAUCSL YoY change (> 3.5%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced risk appetite and earnings discounting. The interaction effect is non-additive.
failure_condition: The interaction term (FEDFUNDS * CPIAUCSL) fails to produce a statistically significant negative correlation with 20-day S&P 500 returns (p > 0.05) in any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In housing market recovery (HOUST YoY growth > 5%), increased construction activity and consumer confidence drive positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through sector rotation into real estate and related industries.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST YoY growth exceeds 5%, or the Rank IC for HOUST YoY growth is below 0.03.
